symptom: ako/mxcli#876 (beta blocker): mxcli-rest's 14 scripts migrated with `fmt --upgrade --header` (0 warnings) and passed `check --references`, then `exec` refused 3 of them under mdl 1, writing nothing ("this change cannot be spliced into the stored flow: the Loop at (1210, 200) changes inside its body"). `diff` already reported `Refused:` (#850); `check -p` said nothing, and under mdl 0 the MDL-V1-REBUILD warning only appeared at exec. Repro: repros2/grow-flow-add-guard (adding a guard clause to a stored stub).
cause: Whether a `create or modify` of a stored flow is spliced, refused (mdl 1) or rebuilt (mdl 0) depends on what is stored, so no parse-time rule can see it; check's project tier ran member drops and type checks but never the splice plan. exec (modifyFlowInPlace) and diff (spliceVerdict) each interpreted planFlowModify's error themselves.
file: mdl/executor/flow_verdict.go, mdl/executor/validate_flow_verdicts.go, mdl/executor/cmd_flow_modify.go, mdl/executor/cmd_diff.go, mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go, cmd/mxcli/cmd_check.go, cmd/mxcli/cmd_fmt.go
fix: One verdict function, decideFlowModify (flow_verdict.go), with the refusal and rebuild-warning wording (flowRefusal, flowRebuildWarning); exec, diff and the new CheckFlowVerdicts all act on it. check -p reports MDL-V1-REBUILD as an error with exec's message under mdl 1 and as exec's warning under mdl 0, and an `alter microflow|nanoflow` exec would refuse as MDL090 (alterFlowContext.plan, extracted from execAlterFlow). Only predicted where the stored project is what exec sees: no earlier statement touches the same flow (create/alter/drop/move/rename), and the declared flow / each fragment builds against the stored project. `fmt --upgrade --header -p` runs the same check on the upgraded script and declines the header for the file, naming each statement; --force-header adds it anyway.
test: mdl/roundtrip/flow_verdict_agreement_test.go (integration, parity suite): TestFlowVerdictAgreement_GrowAGuard (both headers + unchanged control), _EarlierStatementIsNotPredicted, _Alter (MDL090 quoting exec, applied-alter control), _Corpus (every PedApp flow + 12 TestApp flows with loops: description and a loop-body probe under mdl 0/1; check, diff and exec agree; fails if no probe refused); cmd/mxcli TestFmtUpgrade_HeaderDeclinedWhereExecWouldRefuse; mdl/executor TestFlowRebuildRuleIsTheLanguageChange. Revert checks: blanking the verdict in flowModifyViolations makes GrowAGuard report 'check error=false, diff refused=true, exec refused=true'; dropping the alter error fails _Alter; skipping the decline puts the header on the refused script.
insight: A command that predicts another must call the same decision function, not re-derive it: diff and exec had already disagreed once (#839) and check had never asked. When a verdict depends on stored state, the prediction is only valid where the script has not changed that state first, so the guard is part of the feature, and the agreement test must include cases where the verdict is a refusal or it is vacuous.
